lesson.child_mission: Rhythm and timing in movement mean matching actions to a beat; students clap, step and freeze on counts.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same idea to a new game or situation, then compare two choices for safety and inclusion.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Create an 8-count pattern with three different actions.

FEEDBACK
Any clear 8-count with variety.

WATCH FOR
Ignoring the beat makes group dance chaotic.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compose and teach a partner an 8-count rhythm phrase. Perform together.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
lesson.learning_intention: Rhythm and timing in movement mean matching actions to a beat; students clap, step and freeze on counts.
materials: Clear, safe movement space with an adult nearby for any physical activity
Optional: soft ball, cushion or water bottle
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Compose and teach a partner an 8-count rhythm phrase. Perform together. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Any clear 8-count with variety. Reasoning: I used rhythm by attending to timing rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Ignoring the beat makes group dance chaotic. Correction: Any clear 8-count with variety. Why: the correction restores accurate use of rhythm.

Parent: Likely misconception: Ignoring the beat makes group dance chaotic. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating rhythm on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with rhythm, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

teach_steps.explain:
Rhythm and timing in movement mean matching actions to a beat; students clap, step and freeze on counts.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
